description: This is team TITANIUM working on Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data
summary:
FieldWise AI is an open-source agronomic decision-support platform built with FastAPI and React 19 that helps farmers transition from climate-vulnerable monocultures to resilient, water-smart crop rotations. It fuses genuine NASA Earth Observations—30-year NASA POWER agroclimatology (1981–2024), MERRA-2/GLDAS root-zone soil wetness, live NASA GIBS satellite layers (SMAP soil moisture, GPM IMERG precipitation, MODIS Terra NDVI), and 30m SRTM elevation data—with ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 profiles and ICAR regional calendars for 18+ crops.

Directly addressing the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge, FieldWise AI evaluates Baseline Monocultures against Climate-Resilient and Soil-Regenerative rotations across five transparent dimensions: water resilience, soil regeneration, thermal suitability, erosion mitigation, and botanical pest disruption. Interactive farmer priority sliders recalculate rankings in real time, while a climate simulator stress-tests rotations against +1.5°C to +3.0°C warming, -30% droughts, and +25% monsoon deluges.

Continuous monocultures exhaust groundwater, accelerate soil erosion, and suffer 35–50% yield collapses during extreme weather. By translating resolution-honest, zero-fake-data satellite intelligence into actionable cropping plans, FieldWise AI helps farmers conserve water, fix soil nitrogen, and maintain 85–92% yield stability.
details:
What FieldWise AI Does & How It Works FieldWise AI is an open-source agronomic decision-support platform built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge ("Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data") to help farmers transition from climate-vulnerable monocultures to resilient, water-smart crop rotations. Using a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) rotation engine and a climate perturbation simulator, the platform evaluates a farm's Baseline Monoculture against two alternatives—Strategy A (Climate-Resilient) and Strategy B (Soil-Regenerative Leader)—across five transparent agronomic dimensions: Water Resilience, Soil Regeneration, Thermal Suitability, Erosion Mitigation, and Botanical Pest Disruption.

To ground every recommendation in real environmental conditions, FieldWise AI fuses multi-source Earth observations with regional agronomy:

  • NASA POWER & MERRA-2/GLDAS: Ingests 30-year climatological normals (1981–2024) and daily records for precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), temperatures (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN), solar radiation, and root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT).
  • NASA GIBS WMTS Live Layers: Streams real-time SMAP Soil Moisture, GPM IMERG Precipitation Rates, and MODIS Terra 8-day NDVI tiles directly onto interactive farm maps.
  • NASA SRTM DEM: Uses 30m elevation and slope modeling to calculate Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE) runoff and erosion risk.
  • ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 & ICAR Calendars: Combines 250m gridded soil properties (clay, sand, silt, soil organic carbon, pH, bulk density, and CEC) with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) traits for 18+ Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid crops.

Benefits & Intended Impact Continuous monocultures deplete groundwater, leave soil bare to erosion, perpetuate pest cycles, and suffer 35–50% yield collapses during extreme weather. FieldWise AI gives farmers and agricultural advisors a transparent, zero-cost tool to quantify trade-offs before planting. Across four pre-configured Indian agro-ecological hubs—Dharwad (Karnataka), Ludhiana (Punjab), Nagpur (Maharashtra), and Jodhpur (Rajasthan)—diversified legume-millet rotations demonstrated in the platform maintain 85–92% yield stability under climate shocks. For example, transitioning from continuous Cotton–Fallow to Pearl Millet–Chickpea–Summer Moong in Dharwad saves 270 mm of water and fixes 83 kg N/ha, while shifting Rice–Wheat to Maize–Chickpea–Green Gram in Ludhiana reduces water demand by 45%.

Tools, Languages & Software Stack

  • Backend & Scientific Engine: Built with Python (3.10+ / 3.14) and FastAPI, featuring a local caching layer for NASA POWER, SoilGrids v2.0, and SRTM DEM data ingestion, a deterministic MCDA rotation scorer, a climate perturbation engine, and automated pytest verification.
  • Frontend & Geospatial Visualization: Built with React 19, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS v4, integrating Leaflet for live NASA GIBS WMTS map overlays and Recharts for climatology, root-zone soil wetness, and multi-axis radar charts.
  • Deployment Architecture: Packaged for single-command local execution (start.bat, start.ps1, or uvicorn serving an embedded production frontend with interactive OpenAPI/Swagger docs at /docs) alongside a dual-server Vite HMR development mode.

What Makes FieldWise AI Creative Rather than presenting passive satellite imagery or an opaque black-box prediction, FieldWise AI turns multi-sensor NASA data into an interactive, farmer-controlled decision sandbox. Farmers can adjust real-time Decision Priority Sliders (Water, Soil, Net Income, and Climate Resilience) to immediately re-rank crop rotations based on their own household goals, then trigger the Climate What-If Simulator (+1.5°C to +3.0°C warming, -30% drought deficits, +25% monsoon deluges, and compound shocks) to visually test how deep-rooted, nitrogen-fixing rotations buffer yield against extreme weather.

Key Factors Considered

  • Scientific Integrity & Zero Synthetic Data: Eliminated mock or randomized values so every climate envelope, soil profile, and map layer reflects genuine satellite or verified regional observations.
  • Spatial Resolution Honesty: Added dedicated uncertainty and resolution modals to clearly distinguish macro-climatic grids—NASA POWER (~50 km), SMAP (9 km), and GPM IMERG (10 km)—from field-level context in SoilGrids (250 m) and SRTM (30 m).
  • Farmer Economics & Ethical Advisory Scope: Balanced ecological metrics with net income priorities, ensured open access without login barriers, and explicitly framed outputs as decision-support guidance rather than a substitute for certified agronomists or laboratory soil testing.
